body.statement:
For each fixed \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\), there are a class-wide constant \(C_1>0\) and center-dependent constants \(c_0(P_0)>0\) and \(\kappa(P_0)>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\leq C_1\frac{L_n}{n}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{n}{L_n}
\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))}
\mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P)\rVert^2
\geq c_0(P_0).
\]
The lower bound is witnessed by def:green-local-alternatives and lem:green-local-alternatives, for which \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=(\eta/a_h)L_n\).  The upper bound remains the uniform assertion over \(\mathcal F_s\).
body.justification: The testing reduction gives the lower-rate mechanism, while the upper-risk half requires integrated uniform remainder bounds.
body.gap: Weak convergence and deterministic differentiability do not supply the missing second-moment control.
body.consumer: A matched minimax rate is not yet claimed.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove the upper bound.  On the good event from lem:uniform-critical-estimates, use expansion (1) in thm:joint-critical-clt.  Independence, the score second-moment bound, and the bounded cell ratios imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left\lVert
 \sum_g\frac1{n_g}\sum_i\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i})
 \right\rVert^2
 \leq C\frac{L_n}{n}.
\tag{1}
\]
The squared deterministic bias is at most \(Ch_n^{2(s-2)}\leq C/n\), because
\(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\).  The mixed remainder and the fourth-moment pilot bound give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\lVert r_n\rVert^2
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{nh_n^{9/2}}+h_n^{2s-5/2}\right\}^2
 \leq C\frac{L_n}{n},
\tag{2}
\]
where the final inequality uses \(a_h<1/9\).  On the complementary event the translation-aware torus displacement and the measurable fallback are bounded, while (5) of lem:uniform-critical-estimates is exponentially small; its contribution is therefore \(o(L_n/n)\).  Equations (1)--(2) prove the class-uniform upper bound.

For the lower bound, fix the alternatives in lem:green-local-alternatives and let
\[
 \Delta_n=\left|\upsilon^{\mathsf T}
 \{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right|.
\tag{3}
\]
That lemma and \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=\eta\log n=(\eta/a_h)L_n\) give
\[
 \Delta_n^2\geq c(P_0)\zeta^2\frac{L_n}{n}.
\tag{4}
\]
Choose \(\zeta>0\) small enough that the product squared Hellinger distance is at most \(1/2\), and then choose \(\kappa(P_0)\) so that both alternatives belong to
\(\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))\).  If \(Q_{n,+}\) and \(Q_{n,-}\) denote their product sampling laws, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \lVert Q_{n,+}-Q_{n,-}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\operatorname{Hel}(Q_{n,+},Q_{n,-})\leq2^{-1/2}.
\tag{5}
\]
For any estimator \(\widetilde\tau_n\), decide between the two alternatives by whichever value in (3) is closer to
\(\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\widetilde\tau_{n,1}\).  On a wrong decision the squared scalar error is at least \(\Delta_n^2/4\).  The sum of the two testing-error probabilities is at least
\(1-\lVert Q_{n,+}-Q_{n,-}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Since vector squared error dominates the squared projected error,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))}
 E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P)\rVert^2
 \geq\frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}(1-2^{-1/2}).
\tag{6}
\]
Take the infimum over estimators, multiply by \(n/L_n\), use (4), and take the lower limit.  This yields the asserted positive constant \(c_0(P_0)\) and completes the matched upper and lower bounds.
